The overall color palette features soft warm orange tones blended with pink-blue neon reflections as a unifying base. shot1: Shot 1 opens with establishing the scene. A wide eye-level shot slowly pushes in from the neon-lit glass street front to the small stall exterior. A white chef stands behind the counter preparing to start. Warm yellow light spills out from inside, while pink-blue neon reflections blend at the window edge.
shot2: Shot 2 hard-cut from previous shot. Medium close-up overhead view shifts to the countertop. Composition centers the wooden cutting board, places the vegetable basket in the left foreground, and positions a small white porcelain bowl in the right rear to balance empty space. Shallow depth of field keeps focus on hand movements. The chef retrieves bell pepper, mushrooms, and carrot one by one and places them on the board. Ingredients show slight moisture droplets. Warm lighting enhances color saturation. A faint neon edge glow reflects through the glass. The crisp tapping The camera performs a minimal downward tilt and slight push-in to emphasize the beginning of the procedure.
shot3: Shot 3 hard-cut from previous shot. Close-up overhead view focuses on slicing action. Partial uncut vegetables appear in the foreground. Focus rests on the knife edge and safe finger grip. The chef slices bell pepper, mushrooms, and carrot into neat strips in sequence. Ingredients transition from solid blocks to uniform strips. Cuts are fresh and moist. Watercolor texture softens edges slightly but maintains clear outlines. The rhythmic tap-tap The camera makes a small lateral follow movement with the hands to ensure tutorial clarity.
shot4: Shot 4 hard-cut from previous shot. Extreme close-up overhead view focuses on a single clove of garlic and the tip of the knife. Composition is tighter, with blurred vegetable strips in the foreground for layering and a softly blurred stove outline in the background. The chef minces the garlic into fine pieces, building up granules from coarse to fine. Warm light highlights the garlic's slightly moist sheen. The camera remains stable at close range, with only a slight push-in to emphasize garlic mincing.
shot5: Shot 5 hard-cut from previous shot. Medium eye-level shot shifts to the stove. Composition uses the pot rim in the foreground to form an arc framing the subject. Through the glass in the background, flowing neon lights are visible. The chef ignites the flame, places the pot, and pours oil in one smooth motion. Flame erupts from the bottom of the pot. Transparent oil spreads across the black surface, forming a shiny film. Lighting remains warm-dominated, with cold neon reflections on the pot body.
shot6: Shot 6 hard-cut from previous shot. Close-up overhead view into the pot. The pot rim acts as a natural frame. Focus centers on the moment minced garlic hits hot oil. The chef first adds garlic to sizzle. Garlic particles transform from dry to oily and slightly golden. Tiny bubbles rapidly rise. Steam begins to rise. Warm light illuminates the texture inside the pot. The camera briefly dips down then stabilizes to clearly show the reaction process.
shot7: Shot 7 hard-cut from previous shot. Composition places remaining vegetables on the left and stirring ingredients on the right. Focus lies on color changes within the pot. The chef sequentially adds bell pepper, mushrooms, and carrot and quickly stir-fries. Green, off-white, and orange colors are coated in oil under heat. Mushrooms soften, carrots become shinier, and bell peppers shift from crisp to slightly tender. The spatula continuously flips ingredients, lifting them briefly before dropping back. Sleeve and apron edges sway with motion. Sizzling and spatula tapping rhythms grow denser.
shot8: Shot 8 hard-cut from previous shot. Extreme close-up low-angle shot near the pot rim. Composition contrasts the foreground sauce stream with blurred neon background. After adding sauce, the chef quickly tosses the pot to reduce sauce. Dark sauce first gathers at the bottom, then evenly coats the vegetables. Liquid thickens from thin to glossy. When tossed, it forms an arched trajectory. Steam becomes more noticeable but does not obscure the subject. The camera follows the toss with a quick upward surge and return, precisely matching the peak action.
shot9: Shot 9 hard-cut from previous shot. Medium eye-level shot shifts to plating area. Composition places the white plate slightly below center, with pot rim in foreground indicating action origin. Background still shows flowing neon outside the glass. The chef neatly plates the glossy hot dish. Vegetables naturally pile up, forming a full volume. Sauce thinly coats the surface and flows back along the edge. Steam continues to rise. Warm light makes the white plate appear cleaner and the dish more vivid. The The camera slightly pulls back to give the finished dish full contour.
shot10: Shot 10 transitions from previous shot with a soft fade-in/fade-out. Close-up eye-level shot presents the finished dish by the neon window. Composition places the white plate at the lower third intersection. Foreground has slight glass reflection. Background is softened into colored blocks of cyberpunk streetscape. Focus locks on the glossiness of the hot dish and slowly rising steam. The chef holds the plate steadily for a moment. Bell pepper, mushrooms, and carrot display distinct layers under warm light and neon edge glow. The entire dish appears freshly cooked, moist, and vibrant. The camera performs an extremely slow push-in with slight upward tilt, finally stopping on the most appetizing detail of the finished dish.
